props.name: children
props.description: The content, which is also what the skeleton is drawn from. Renders the data, or the sample the skeleton is drawn from.

props.name: data
props.description: The data to show. The skeleton shows while it is `null` or `undefined`.

props.name: label
props.description: Read to screen readers while loading, in place of the skeleton, such as "Loading invoices". Defaults to the locale dictionary's "Loading".

props.name: loading
props.description: Shows the skeleton drawn from `children` instead of `children` themselves. Shows the skeleton over `data` too, as for a refetch. It is drawn from the data on screen.

props.name: onReveal
props.description: Called once content has come in over a skeleton and finished arriving. A reveal interrupted by loading again, or by unmounting, does not call it. One that Suspense or a hidden `Activity` interrupted, or that came due while hidden, finishes at once when the reveal shows again and calls it then; one that a later load replaced while hidden does not.

props.name: render
props.description: Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render.

props.name: reveal
props.description: How content replaces the skeleton. `smart`, the default, holds a client skeleton back 150 ms so a fast load never shows one, lands content at once over a skeleton that was up only a moment or while someone scrolls or types, crossfades a refetch and small content, and brings larger content in row by row. `together` crossfades it all at once; `sequence` brings each piece in by its place, top to bottom and then a little left to right.

props.name: sample
props.description: Stands in for `data` to draw the skeleton before any data has loaded.
